title: Federal Records and Joe Assunto
summary: He recorded four sides for King's Federal label; Joe Assunto handled business; he got session fees but no royalties.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Yeah. That was King's label. Yeah. But, uh...
Yeah, King had that. Yeah. Who was head... Who... Did somebody come from out of town?
Who did I do that for? Federal.
I don't know, Joe Santo at that time was conducting the business part of the situation. Joe Santo was conducting the business.

The one-stop record shop. Yeah, on Rampart. So I never asked questions, like I said. The only questions I'd ask is the one that's doing right. Them's the ones I want to know, you know. Yeah. If it's not worth it in my mind and in my head, it's no sense of me learning whose names it was, because I wasn't going to affiliate nothing they were doing no more anyway.
So you did, but you did, let's see, there were four songs for Federal. Four. Rockin' With Fest and Gone So Long was the... Yeah. So you must have, were you paid for that session, like the other ones?
You always got a session fee up front, but you never got any royalties afterwards. So they would always pay for the session and for the musicians.
That was the end of it, as far as I was concerned. Now I did another thing with Elps. Elps.
